text:
STL comes in off a 4-1 win over BOS two days ago, 3-2-0 in its last five, and is missing Ross Johnston and Dillon Dube. It is also game one of a four-game road trip. DET beat CHI by the same 4-1 score, with Viktor Arvidsson scoring three goals, and is 3-1-1 over its last five. The Red Wings are without Dylan Larkin, who is serving a suspension, and the minutes he left behind have gone to Alex DeBrincat beside Lucas Raymond and Arvidsson, with Emmitt Finnie on the first power-play unit. Two old faces return: Jonatan Berggren is back in Detroit for the first time since leaving the Red Wings, and Justin Faulk faces the Blues for the first time since leaving them.

In our numbers, DET has the better of play at five on five, with 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) against 50% for STL. The Red Wings have 54% of the expected goals overall but a -1 goal difference, because their finishing has run well below what their chances usually produce. They also take 4.2 penalties a game, and their power play (0.86 expected goals a game) beats STL's (0.49). In net, projected starter Joel Hofer sits at +4.9 goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie has stopped beyond what his shots should allow) this season, while projected DET starter John Gibson is at -3.7, though Gibson was +10.1 last year.

Our model gives the home side a slight edge, 3.00 expected goals to 2.81. DeBrincat and Arvidsson each have a 36% chance to score, and Raymond 31%. For STL, Mason McTavish is at 27%. Pius Suter, one assist from 100 career assists, is also worth a look.
